poolName: Networking & Edge: Route 53, Global Accelerator, CloudFront, Shield, WAF, API Gateway, Firewall Manager & AppSync (Mixed Difficulty)
description: SAA-C03 revision questions on Amazon Route 53, AWS Global Accelerator, Amazon CloudFront, Lambda@Edge and CloudFront Functions, AWS Shield, AWS WAF, Amazon API Gateway, AWS Firewall Manager and AWS AppSync at Easy, Medium and Hard difficulty: routing policies, edge delivery and acceleration, DDoS and web exploit protection, API types and trade-offs, and GraphQL.

questions.prompt: A company wants DNS records that are resolved only by resources inside its VPCs and are not visible on the public internet. Which Route 53 construct should it create?
choices: A health check
A traffic policy record
A private hosted zone
A public hosted zone
questions.correctChoice: A private hosted zone
questions.explanation: A private hosted zone holds records that answer queries only from the VPCs it is associated with. A public hosted zone routes internet traffic.

questions.prompt: A company must point the zone apex of its domain (example.com) at an Application Load Balancer. Which record type should it use?
choices: A TXT record containing the load balancer DNS name
An alias A record pointing at the load balancer
An MX record pointing at the load balancer DNS name
A CNAME record pointing at the load balancer DNS name
questions.correctChoice: An alias A record pointing at the load balancer
questions.explanation: A CNAME is not permitted at the zone apex. An alias record can be created at the apex, is dynamically tied to the AWS endpoint, and survives IP changes of the underlying resource.

questions.prompt: Which of the following can be used directly as the target of a Route 53 alias record?
choices: An Amazon RDS DB instance endpoint
An Amazon EBS volume ID
An AWS Lambda function ARN
An S3 static website endpoint
questions.correctChoice: An S3 static website endpoint
questions.explanation: Alias records can point at AWS endpoints such as CloudFront distributions, load balancers, Elastic Beanstalk environments, S3 website endpoints, VPC endpoints and API Gateway custom regional APIs.

questions.prompt: Which Route 53 routing policy sends traffic to a primary resource and switches to a secondary resource only when health checks on the primary fail?
choices: Multi-value answer
Failover
Geolocation
Weighted
questions.correctChoice: Failover
questions.explanation: Failover routing is active-passive. Route 53 monitors the primary with a health check and begins answering with the secondary when the primary is unhealthy.

questions.prompt: A team wants to send roughly 10% of DNS responses to a new application version and 90% to the current version. Which routing policy fits best?
choices: Latency-based
Weighted
Geolocation
Simple
questions.correctChoice: Weighted
questions.explanation: Weighted routing assigns a relative weight to each record, so the share of responses matches the weights. It is commonly used for gradual rollouts and A/B tests.

questions.prompt: An application runs in two Regions behind ALBs. Each user should be directed to whichever Region gives them the lowest latency. Which routing policy should be used?
choices: Failover
Weighted
Latency-based
IP-based
questions.correctChoice: Latency-based
questions.explanation: Latency-based routing needs a latency record for the resource in each Region and answers with the Region that has the lowest latency for the user.

questions.prompt: By default, how often does Route 53 perform each health check request, and what faster interval can be configured?
choices: Every 60 seconds by default; it can be reduced to every 30 seconds
Every 30 seconds by default; it can be reduced to every 10 seconds
Every 10 seconds by default; it can be reduced to every 1 second
Every 5 minutes by default; it can be reduced to every 1 minute
questions.correctChoice: Every 30 seconds by default; it can be reduced to every 10 seconds
questions.explanation: Route 53 health checks run every 30 seconds by default, with a fast option of 10 seconds.

questions.prompt: Which Route 53 Resolver endpoint type allows DNS queries to originate on an on-premises network and be resolved inside a VPC?
choices: Outbound endpoint
Gateway endpoint
Inbound endpoint
Interface endpoint for Route 53
questions.correctChoice: Inbound endpoint
questions.explanation: Inbound Resolver endpoints receive DNS queries coming into the VPC from on premises or another VPC. Outbound endpoints send queries out of the VPC.

questions.prompt: What does enabling DNSSEC signing for a Route 53 public hosted zone allow DNS resolvers to do?
choices: Block DNS queries that originate from malicious IP addresses
Encrypt the DNS queries sent from clients to Route 53
Automatically fail over to a secondary Region when the primary fails
Validate that a DNS response came from Route 53 and has not been tampered with
questions.correctChoice: Validate that a DNS response came from Route 53 and has not been tampered with
questions.explanation: DNSSEC provides origin authentication and integrity for DNS responses, which protects against impersonation and tampering. It does not encrypt queries or provide failover.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of Route 53 Profiles?
choices: To register new domain names and transfer existing domains between registrars
To monitor the health of endpoints and send notifications when a health check fails
To apply DNS-related configuration, such as private hosted zones and Resolver rules, across multiple VPCs and accounts
To route each DNS query to whichever endpoint currently gives the user the lowest network latency
questions.correctChoice: To apply DNS-related configuration, such as private hosted zones and Resolver rules, across multiple VPCs and accounts
questions.explanation: Profiles let you associate private hosted zones, Resolver rules and DNS Firewall rule groups once and apply them to many VPCs and AWS accounts.

questions.prompt: A streaming company must serve users in Germany from a Frankfurt deployment because of content licensing and data residency rules, even if another Region has lower latency for some of those users. Which routing policy meets this?
choices: Weighted
Geolocation
Failover
Latency-based
questions.correctChoice: Geolocation
questions.explanation: Geolocation routes by the user's location, so the rule is applied regardless of latency. Latency-based routing optimises for speed and could send users to another Region.

questions.prompt: A company has endpoints in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 and wants users routed to the geographically closest endpoint. After scaling up us-east-1, it wants that Region to serve a larger geographic area, including some users who are physically closer to Europe, without writing country-by-country rules. Which solution meets this?
choices: Weighted routing with 70% on us-east-1 and 30% on eu-west-1
Latency-based routing with a latency record in each Region
Geoproximity routing with a positive bias on the us-east-1 record
Geolocation routing with a record for every country
questions.correctChoice: Geoproximity routing with a positive bias on the us-east-1 record
questions.explanation: Geoproximity routes by user and resource location and lets you expand or shrink a Region's effective area with a bias. Weighted routing ignores location, and geolocation requires explicit location mappings.

questions.prompt: A simple routing record returns the IP addresses of three web servers. When one server fails, some clients intermittently time out. The company does not want to add a load balancer. What is the best change?
choices: Replace the record with a failover record pair using all three servers
Replace the record with weighted records with equal weights and no health checks
Increase the TTL of the simple record
Replace the record with multi-value answer records, each with a health check
questions.correctChoice: Replace the record with multi-value answer records, each with a health check
questions.explanation: Simple routing has no health checking, so failed servers are still returned. Multi-value answer routing returns only healthy addresses. Equal weights without health checks would still return failed servers.

questions.prompt: When a Route 53 health check detects an unhealthy endpoint, which actions can it drive?
choices: It can trigger DNS failover and create a CloudWatch alarm to notify operators
It can restart the instance and replace the failed EBS volume
It can resize the Auto Scaling group and add capacity
It can rotate the TLS certificate and reissue it
questions.correctChoice: It can trigger DNS failover and create a CloudWatch alarm to notify operators
questions.explanation: Route 53 health checks influence DNS answers for failover and can be tied to CloudWatch alarms for notification. They do not repair or scale resources.

questions.prompt: A service is considered healthy only if at least two of its three component endpoints pass their own health checks. When it is unhealthy, DNS must fail over to a DR site. How should this be configured?
choices: Create a health check that monitors the three component health checks with a threshold of two, and associate it with the primary failover record
Create three separate failover records, one for each component endpoint, with the same name
Associate only one component's health check with the primary failover record and ignore the others
Create a weighted record for each component with equal weights and a shared health check
questions.correctChoice: Create a health check that monitors the three component health checks with a threshold of two, and associate it with the primary failover record
questions.explanation: A health check that monitors other health checks combines their results against a threshold. Associating it with the primary failover record triggers failover when the service as a whole is unhealthy.

questions.prompt: Many VPCs across several accounts must resolve names in the on-premises corporate domain over Direct Connect, and the network team wants this configured once and consistently applied. Which design is appropriate?
choices: An inbound Resolver endpoint in every VPC with a forwarding rule for the corporate domain
An outbound Resolver endpoint with a forwarding rule for the corporate domain, applied to the VPCs through a Route 53 Profile
A latency-based record for each on-premises DNS server in the corporate network
A public hosted zone containing the corporate records, associated with every VPC
questions.correctChoice: An outbound Resolver endpoint with a forwarding rule for the corporate domain, applied to the VPCs through a Route 53 Profile
questions.explanation: Queries leaving a VPC for on-premises DNS use an outbound endpoint and a forwarding rule. A Profile can apply the Resolver rule to many VPCs and accounts.

questions.prompt: On-premises servers must resolve hostnames in a Route 53 private hosted zone that is associated with a VPC. What should be configured?
choices: An inbound Resolver endpoint that the on-premises DNS servers forward queries to
An outbound Resolver endpoint in the VPC with a forwarding rule for the domain
A public hosted zone with the same domain name as the private hosted zone
A Route 53 health check on each of the on-premises DNS servers
questions.correctChoice: An inbound Resolver endpoint that the on-premises DNS servers forward queries to
questions.explanation: On-premises DNS servers forward queries to the IP addresses of an inbound Resolver endpoint, which resolves them in the VPC, including private hosted zone records.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes Route 53 Traffic Flow?
choices: It provides a visual editor for building complex routing configurations and supports versioning of traffic policies
It is a free feature that automatically replaces all Route 53 health checks
It automatically caches DNS answers at CloudFront edge locations worldwide
It encrypts DNS traffic between the client and the recursive resolver
questions.correctChoice: It provides a visual editor for building complex routing configurations and supports versioning of traffic policies
questions.explanation: Traffic Flow lets you build and version sophisticated routing policies in a UI, and it is charged per policy record.

questions.prompt: What does Route 53 Application Recovery Controller zonal shift do?
choices: Moves load balancer traffic away from an impaired Availability Zone toward healthy ones
Fails an RDS database over to its standby instance in another Availability Zone
Replicates a hosted zone to a second Region so that DNS keeps working during a Region failure
Moves EC2 instances to a different Availability Zone automatically when one is impaired
questions.correctChoice: Moves load balancer traffic away from an impaired Availability Zone toward healthy ones
questions.explanation: Zonal shift temporarily shifts traffic for a supported ALB or NLB away from an impaired AZ. It does not move instances or databases.

questions.prompt: A security team is concerned that attackers could impersonate the company's domain by forging DNS responses sent to users. Which Route 53 capability addresses this specific risk?
choices: Enable Route 53 health checks with a 10-second interval
Enable DNSSEC signing on the public hosted zone
Attach AWS WAF to the hosted zone
Create a private hosted zone with the same name
questions.correctChoice: Enable DNSSEC signing on the public hosted zone
questions.explanation: DNSSEC lets resolvers validate that responses really came from Route 53 and were not altered, which stops forged answers. WAF filters HTTP requests and does not protect DNS responses.

questions.prompt: An application is deployed active-active in two Regions behind ALBs. Users should normally reach the Region with the lowest latency, and if one Region becomes unhealthy all users must be sent to the other Region automatically. Which DNS design meets this?
choices: Two failover records, with each Region marked as the primary
Weighted records with a 50/50 split and no health checks
Latency-based alias records for each Region's ALB, each associated with a health check
Geolocation records for each continent without a default record
questions.correctChoice: Latency-based alias records for each Region's ALB, each associated with a health check
questions.explanation: Latency-based routing gives lowest-latency answers and, with health checks on the records, Route 53 stops returning an unhealthy Region. Failover is active-passive and would not serve both Regions normally.

questions.prompt: A company created geolocation records only for the United States and Europe. Users in other countries receive no usable DNS answer. What is the simplest fix?
choices: Replace all of the records with a single simple routing record containing every IP address
Add a default geolocation record to answer queries from locations that match no other record
Increase the health check interval to 10 seconds so that failures are detected sooner
Create a private hosted zone with the same name for the users in the other countries
questions.correctChoice: Add a default geolocation record to answer queries from locations that match no other record
questions.explanation: Geolocation routing needs a default record to answer queries from locations not covered by a specific record. Without it, Route 53 returns no answer for those users.

questions.prompt: A central network team manages 50 VPCs across 12 AWS accounts. They want the same private hosted zone associations, Resolver forwarding rules and DNS Firewall rule groups applied consistently, with minimal per-VPC work. What should they use?
choices: A Route 53 Profile associated with the VPCs
An AWS Global Accelerator accelerator for each VPC
Route 53 Traffic Flow with a traffic policy for each account
Manual association of each resource with every VPC, one at a time
questions.correctChoice: A Route 53 Profile associated with the VPCs
questions.explanation: A Profile bundles private hosted zones, Resolver rules and DNS Firewall rule groups so they can be associated once with many VPCs and shared across accounts.

questions.prompt: Which statement about zonal shift in Route 53 Application Recovery Controller is correct?
choices: It supports ALBs and NLBs, and shifts traffic away from a single Availability Zone per load balancer
It supports an ALB used as an endpoint of an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator
It supports only Classic Load Balancers with cross-zone load balancing disabled
It can shift traffic away from several Availability Zones of one load balancer at once
questions.correctChoice: It supports ALBs and NLBs, and shifts traffic away from a single Availability Zone per load balancer
questions.explanation: Zonal shift works with ALBs and NLBs (cross-zone enabled or disabled), only one AZ per load balancer at a time, and not for an ALB that is a Global Accelerator endpoint.

questions.prompt: On-premises servers must resolve names in a VPC private hosted zone, and VPC workloads must resolve names in the on-premises corporate domain. Connectivity is already in place over Direct Connect. What is the minimum Route 53 Resolver setup?
choices: One inbound endpoint and one outbound endpoint, with a forwarding rule for the on-premises domain
Two outbound endpoints, one in each Availability Zone
A single inbound endpoint with a forwarding rule for the on-premises domain
A single outbound endpoint and a public hosted zone for the corporate domain
questions.correctChoice: One inbound endpoint and one outbound endpoint, with a forwarding rule for the on-premises domain
questions.explanation: Each direction needs its own endpoint type: inbound for on-premises to VPC queries and outbound with a forwarding rule for VPC to on-premises queries.

questions.prompt: A company wants clients from specific ISP network ranges, defined as CIDR blocks, to be sent to a particular endpoint to improve performance. Which Route 53 routing policy fits?
choices: Geolocation routing
IP-based routing
Multi-value answer routing
Simple routing
questions.correctChoice: IP-based routing
questions.explanation: IP-based routing uses CIDR ranges that you define for client IP addresses, unlike geolocation which uses the user's geographic location.

questions.prompt: A web application runs on an ALB in one Region. If it fails, users should see a static maintenance page hosted in an S3 website bucket. Which approach should be used?
choices: Latency-based routing between the ALB and the S3 website endpoint, with no health check
Weighted routing with 100% weight on the ALB and 0% on the S3 endpoint, with no health check
Multi-value answer routing that returns both the ALB and the S3 endpoint at the same time
Failover routing with an alias to the ALB as primary, an alias to the S3 website endpoint as secondary, and a health check on the primary
questions.correctChoice: Failover routing with an alias to the ALB as primary, an alias to the S3 website endpoint as secondary, and a health check on the primary
questions.explanation: Failover routing is active-passive: the secondary is returned only when the health check on the primary fails. An S3 website endpoint is a valid alias target.

questions.prompt: What does AWS Global Accelerator do for an application?
choices: It translates DNS names into IP addresses for resources that run inside a VPC
It caches static objects at edge locations so that fewer requests reach the origin
It sends user traffic to the nearest AWS edge location and over the AWS network to the optimal healthy endpoint
It inspects HTTP requests at the edge and blocks SQL injection attempts
questions.correctChoice: It sends user traffic to the nearest AWS edge location and over the AWS network to the optimal healthy endpoint
questions.explanation: Global Accelerator brings traffic onto the AWS global network at an edge location and routes it to the best healthy endpoint. CDN caching is CloudFront and request filtering is WAF.

questions.prompt: Which Global Accelerator type maps individual users to specific EC2 instance and port destinations within VPC subnets?
choices: Standard accelerator
Edge-optimised accelerator
Regional accelerator
Custom routing accelerator
questions.correctChoice: Custom routing accelerator
questions.explanation: Custom routing accelerators map users to specific instance and port destinations in VPC subnets. Standard accelerators route to the nearest healthy endpoint.

questions.prompt: Which of the following can be an endpoint for a standard Global Accelerator accelerator?
choices: An Amazon S3 bucket
An Application Load Balancer
An Amazon RDS DB instance
An Amazon DynamoDB table
questions.correctChoice: An Application Load Balancer
questions.explanation: Standard accelerator endpoints are Application Load Balancers, Network Load Balancers, EC2 instances and Elastic IP addresses.

questions.prompt: A UDP-based game must have fixed IP addresses that players' firewalls can allow-list, low-latency access, and automatic redirection away from an unhealthy Region. Servers sit behind Network Load Balancers in two Regions. Which solution meets this?
choices: Global Accelerator with the NLBs as endpoints in endpoint groups for each Region
An edge-optimised API Gateway REST API in front of the NLBs
Route 53 latency-based records with a short TTL
A CloudFront distribution with both NLBs as origins
questions.correctChoice: Global Accelerator with the NLBs as endpoints in endpoint groups for each Region
questions.explanation: Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses, supports UDP and shifts traffic away from unhealthy endpoints. CloudFront is HTTP(S)-oriented and DNS-based failover does not give fixed IPs.

questions.prompt: An operator wants to shift traffic gradually away from a Region's endpoint group during maintenance, without removing the endpoints. Which Global Accelerator feature helps?
choices: A new Route 53 hosted zone
An additional origin in a CloudFront distribution
A listener on a different port
The traffic dial on the endpoint group
questions.correctChoice: The traffic dial on the endpoint group
questions.explanation: Each endpoint group in a Region has a traffic dial that controls the percentage of traffic it receives, so traffic can be reduced or drained without deleting endpoints.

questions.prompt: A company runs an application in two Regions. Clients are hard-coded to a fixed set of IP addresses and some resolvers cache DNS answers well beyond the TTL. The company needs fast failover to the healthy Region. What should it do?
choices: Use Route 53 failover records with a low TTL so that resolvers refresh quickly
Use Route 53 weighted records and update the weights manually during an incident
Use a CloudFront distribution that has both Regions configured as origins
Use Global Accelerator, which provides static anycast IP addresses and routes around unhealthy endpoints
questions.correctChoice: Use Global Accelerator, which provides static anycast IP addresses and routes around unhealthy endpoints
questions.explanation: Global Accelerator gives fixed anycast IP addresses and shifts traffic itself, so failover does not depend on clients or resolvers honouring DNS TTLs.

questions.prompt: A game company assigns each match to a specific EC2 instance and port in a VPC subnet. Players must be deterministically routed to the instance hosting their match using the accelerator. Which option meets this?
choices: A Route 53 geolocation record for each match
A standard accelerator with an ALB endpoint and weighted routing
A CloudFront distribution with a custom origin per match
A custom routing accelerator
questions.correctChoice: A custom routing accelerator
questions.explanation: Custom routing accelerators let the application deterministically map users to specific destinations, which standard accelerators and load balancers do not do.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of Amazon CloudFront?
choices: To block DDoS attacks at the network layer only, without caching any content
To balance traffic across EC2 instances in a single Region and Availability Zone
To deliver content with low latency by caching it at edge locations close to users
To provide a managed DNS service with health checks and several routing policies
questions.correctChoice: To deliver content with low latency by caching it at edge locations close to users
questions.explanation: CloudFront is a content delivery network that caches content in a distributed network of edge locations to speed up delivery.

questions.prompt: A company serves content to users through CloudFront from an Amazon S3 bucket and wants users to access it only through CloudFront, not directly from S3. What should be configured?
choices: Origin Access Control (OAC) on the S3 origin, with a bucket policy allowing CloudFront
An inbound security group rule on the bucket that only allows CloudFront traffic
A public bucket policy that allows s3:GetObject to every principal on the internet
An Elastic IP address that is attached to the bucket and allow-listed on the distribution
questions.correctChoice: Origin Access Control (OAC) on the S3 origin, with a bucket policy allowing CloudFront
questions.explanation: OAC lets CloudFront sign requests to S3 so the bucket can stay private and only be read via the distribution.

questions.prompt: In CloudFront, what is a distribution?
choices: A Route 53 hosted zone that contains the alias records pointing at CloudFront
A Lambda function that rewrites viewer requests before the cache lookup occurs
The configuration that defines how content from origins is cached and delivered through edge locations
A group of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group that runs the origin application
questions.correctChoice: The configuration that defines how content from origins is cached and delivered through edge locations
questions.explanation: A distribution is the CloudFront resource that defines origins and how cached content should behave across the edge network.

questions.prompt: An architect states that CloudFront is only useful for static files. Which response is most accurate?
choices: CloudFront can also deliver dynamic content, video streaming and WebSocket traffic
Correct, because CloudFront cannot connect to EC2 or load balancers
Correct, because CloudFront can only cache objects stored in S3
Partially correct, because dynamic content requires Global Accelerator instead
questions.correctChoice: CloudFront can also deliver dynamic content, video streaming and WebSocket traffic
questions.explanation: CloudFront supports static and dynamic content, video streaming and WebSockets, and can use S3, EC2, ELB or other custom origins.

questions.prompt: Which statement about restricting access to an S3 origin in CloudFront is correct?
choices: Neither can be used with S3 buckets that are encrypted
Origin Access Control is the current approach and Origin Access Identity is the legacy approach
Both require the S3 bucket to be publicly readable
Origin Access Identity is the current approach and Origin Access Control is the legacy approach
questions.correctChoice: Origin Access Control is the current approach and Origin Access Identity is the legacy approach
questions.explanation: OAC supersedes the legacy OAI for keeping S3 origins private.

questions.prompt: What is the role of a regional edge cache in CloudFront?
choices: It sits between edge locations and the origin and holds content longer to reduce requests that reach the origin
It replaces edge locations by serving all viewer requests from a few large Regions
It stores the distribution's access logs permanently for later compliance review
It runs the origin application in a Region close to users to reduce round trips
questions.correctChoice: It sits between edge locations and the origin and holds content longer to reduce requests that reach the origin
questions.explanation: Regional edge caches are larger caches in broad geographic locations that speed up requests from edge locations and reduce load on the origin.

questions.prompt: A company wants to protect a CloudFront-delivered web application against common web exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting. What should it do?
choices: Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the CloudFront distribution
Configure a Route 53 failover record
Create a security group on the distribution
Enable AWS Shield Standard only, which blocks all application attacks
questions.correctChoice: Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the CloudFront distribution
questions.explanation: AWS WAF can be attached to CloudFront and uses rules to block patterns such as injection and XSS in HTTP requests. Shield Standard is focused on network and transport layer DDoS.

questions.prompt: An origin for a CloudFront distribution is an Application Load Balancer. Which configuration type is used for this origin?
choices: A Lambda@Edge origin configuration
An S3 origin configuration
An Elastic IP origin configuration
A custom origin configuration
questions.correctChoice: A custom origin configuration
questions.explanation: Non-S3 origins such as ALBs, EC2 instances and S3 website endpoints are configured as custom origins.

questions.prompt: A static website is served through CloudFront using the S3 website endpoint as a custom origin. The security team now requires the bucket to be private and accessible only through CloudFront. What is the correct approach?
choices: Keep the website endpoint origin and enable OAC on it
Keep the website endpoint and make the bucket public with a long random bucket name
Keep the website endpoint origin and use a legacy OAI
Change the origin to the S3 REST endpoint of the bucket and use OAC with a bucket policy
questions.correctChoice: Change the origin to the S3 REST endpoint of the bucket and use OAC with a bucket policy
questions.explanation: OAC does not apply to S3 website endpoints, which are custom origins. To keep the bucket private, use the S3 REST endpoint as an S3 origin with OAC (index document handling must then be addressed in CloudFront).

questions.prompt: In what order do the four Lambda@Edge event types occur for a request that is not served from the cache?
choices: Viewer request, origin request, origin response, viewer response
Viewer request, viewer response, origin request, origin response
Origin request, origin response, viewer request, viewer response
Origin request, viewer request, viewer response, origin response
questions.correctChoice: Viewer request, origin request, origin response, viewer response
questions.explanation: The viewer request triggers first, then the origin request, the origin response, and finally the viewer response before the response is returned to the user.

questions.prompt: Which languages are supported for CloudFront Functions and Lambda@Edge functions respectively?
choices: CloudFront Functions: Python only; Lambda@Edge: JavaScript only
Both: Java and Go only
CloudFront Functions: JavaScript only; Lambda@Edge: Node.js and Python
CloudFront Functions: Node.js and Python; Lambda@Edge: JavaScript only
questions.correctChoice: CloudFront Functions: JavaScript only; Lambda@Edge: Node.js and Python
questions.explanation: CloudFront Functions are written in JavaScript. Lambda@Edge supports Node.js and Python.

questions.prompt: Which CloudFront events can trigger a CloudFront Function?
choices: Origin request and origin response
Origin response only
Viewer request and viewer response
All four: viewer request, origin request, origin response and viewer response
questions.correctChoice: Viewer request and viewer response
questions.explanation: CloudFront Functions run only on viewer-facing events, whereas Lambda@Edge also supports the origin request and origin response events.

questions.prompt: A site receives millions of requests per second and needs simple header manipulation and URL redirects with sub-millisecond execution at the lowest possible cost. Which option is the best fit?
choices: Lambda@Edge on origin events
CloudFront Functions on viewer events
An EC2 Auto Scaling group running a reverse proxy
An AWS Lambda function behind an Application Load Balancer
questions.correctChoice: CloudFront Functions on viewer events
questions.explanation: CloudFront Functions are lightweight, cheaper and faster than Lambda@Edge and scale to millions of requests per second for simple viewer-side transformations.

questions.prompt: An edge function must call an external HTTPS API and read the request body before deciding how to handle a request. Which option supports this?
choices: Lambda@Edge, because it has network access and request body access
CloudFront Functions, because they run on the largest memory configuration
Neither, because edge functions cannot make network calls
CloudFront Functions, because they have network and request body access
questions.correctChoice: Lambda@Edge, because it has network access and request body access
questions.explanation: CloudFront Functions have no network, file system or request body access. Lambda@Edge supports them, at higher cost and latency.

questions.prompt: A company wants to add security headers such as HSTS and CSP to every response returned to the viewer. At which point should the function run?
choices: On the origin request event
On the viewer request event, before CloudFront checks the cache
On the viewer request event
On the viewer response event
questions.correctChoice: On the viewer response event
questions.explanation: Headers that apply to what the viewer receives are set on the viewer response event, just before CloudFront returns the response.

questions.prompt: A company needs to rewrite request URLs and inject an authentication header just before CloudFront forwards a request to the origin. Which Lambda@Edge event type is appropriate?
choices: Viewer request, because it runs only on cache misses
Viewer response
Origin request
Origin response
questions.correctChoice: Origin request
questions.explanation: The origin request event occurs before CloudFront forwards a request to the origin, which makes it suitable for URL rewrites and origin authentication headers.

questions.prompt: Where do Lambda@Edge functions and CloudFront Functions run?
choices: Both in the origin Region
Lambda@Edge at edge locations; CloudFront Functions in regional edge caches
Both in the user's VPC
Lambda@Edge in regional edge caches; CloudFront Functions at edge locations
questions.correctChoice: Lambda@Edge in regional edge caches; CloudFront Functions at edge locations
questions.explanation: CloudFront Functions run at the edge locations closest to viewers, while Lambda@Edge functions run in regional edge caches.

questions.prompt: A high-traffic site has a poor cache hit ratio because clients send query strings in different orders. The company wants to normalise requests before CloudFront checks its cache, at the lowest cost and latency. Which solution fits?
choices: A Lambda function in the origin Region that normalises requests
A Lambda@Edge function on the origin request event
A CloudFront Function on the viewer request event
An AWS WAF rule that sorts query strings
questions.correctChoice: A CloudFront Function on the viewer request event
questions.explanation: Cache key normalisation must happen on the viewer request, before the cache lookup. CloudFront Functions are suited to this high-scale, lightweight task, and origin request events run only after a cache miss.

questions.prompt: Before serving protected content, a CloudFront distribution must validate each request by calling an external identity provider's API over HTTPS. Which approach is correct?
choices: A CloudFront Function on the viewer response event
A Lambda@Edge function on the viewer response event
A Lambda@Edge function on the viewer request event
A CloudFront Function on the viewer request event
questions.correctChoice: A Lambda@Edge function on the viewer request event
questions.explanation: Calling an external API requires network access, which CloudFront Functions lack. The check must run on the viewer request, before content is served, which is why viewer response is too late.

questions.prompt: The origin returns responses with caching headers that do not match what the company wants, and the corrected headers should apply to the object stored in the CloudFront cache. Where should the headers be modified?
choices: In a CloudFront Function on the viewer request event
In a Lambda@Edge viewer response function
In an AWS WAF rule on the distribution
In a Lambda@Edge origin response function
questions.correctChoice: In a Lambda@Edge origin response function
questions.explanation: The origin response event runs after the origin responds and before the object is cached, so header changes (such as cache control) affect what is cached. Viewer response runs on every response.

questions.prompt: A small company serves its website through CloudFront and Route 53 and wants baseline protection against common network and transport layer DDoS attacks at no extra cost. What should it do?
choices: Nothing extra, because AWS Shield Standard is automatically included at no additional charge
Deploy AWS Firewall Manager policies in every Region before any DDoS protection applies
Purchase a Shield Advanced subscription and then cancel it after the first month
Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced, because Standard is not enabled by default for any resource
questions.correctChoice: Nothing extra, because AWS Shield Standard is automatically included at no additional charge
questions.explanation: Shield Standard is free and automatically applied to all AWS customers, with extra protection when traffic goes through services such as CloudFront and Route 53.

questions.prompt: Which combination provides protection against application-layer (layer 7) DDoS attacks on a web application?
choices: Amazon Route 53 health checks
AWS Firewall Manager alone
AWS Shield with AWS WAF
AWS Shield Standard alone, with no other services
questions.correctChoice: AWS Shield with AWS WAF
questions.explanation: Layer 3 and 4 attacks are handled by Shield, while application-layer protection is achieved through integration with AWS WAF rules.

questions.prompt: Which capabilities are provided by AWS Shield Advanced but not by Shield Standard?
choices: Cross-Region replication of databases and object storage for disaster recovery purposes
Managed encryption of data at rest using customer managed KMS keys in each account
DDoS cost protection, access to the DDoS response team, and detailed attack visibility and reporting
Free, automatic protection that is applied to every AWS service without a subscription
questions.correctChoice: DDoS cost protection, access to the DDoS response team, and detailed attack visibility and reporting
questions.explanation: Shield Advanced is a paid subscription that adds visibility and reporting, support from AWS's response team, DDoS cost protection and an SLA.

questions.prompt: Which of the following resources can be protected by AWS Shield Advanced?
choices: An AWS Global Accelerator accelerator
An Amazon S3 bucket
An AWS Lambda function
An Amazon RDS DB instance
questions.correctChoice: An AWS Global Accelerator accelerator
questions.explanation: Shield Advanced protects Route 53, CloudFront, Elastic Load Balancing, Global Accelerator and Elastic IP addresses (including EC2 and NLB).

questions.prompt: An online retailer runs a public ALB-based application and has suffered large DDoS events. It requires 24/7 access to AWS DDoS specialists, protection against scaling charges during an attack, and application-layer rule tuning. Which solution meets these needs?
choices: Use AWS Shield Standard and AWS Firewall Manager only
Use AWS Network Firewall with no Shield subscription
Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced and use AWS WAF with the protected resources
Rely on AWS Shield Standard and add security group rules
questions.correctChoice: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced and use AWS WAF with the protected resources
questions.explanation: Specialist support and DDoS cost protection are Shield Advanced features, and AWS WAF provides application-layer rules. Shield Standard has neither.

questions.prompt: What does AWS WAF protect web applications from?
choices: Data loss, by replicating objects between Regions and keeping versions of them
Unauthorised AWS API calls, by evaluating IAM identity and resource policies
Common web exploits, by allowing or denying requests based on HTTP request contents
Slow DNS resolution, by caching records in the resolvers close to the users
questions.correctChoice: Common web exploits, by allowing or denying requests based on HTTP request contents
questions.explanation: AWS WAF lets you create rules that inspect HTTP requests and allow or block them, helping to protect against exploits such as injection and cross-site scripting.

questions.prompt: A security team wants to block requests whose query string contains SQL injection patterns. Which control can do this?
choices: AWS WAF rules on the web ACL
An Amazon Route 53 routing policy
A network ACL rule on the subnet
A security group rule on the ALB
questions.correctChoice: AWS WAF rules on the web ACL
questions.explanation: Security groups and network ACLs filter on IP, port and protocol. WAF inspects HTTP request contents such as the query string, headers and body.

questions.prompt: A team wants ready-made WAF rules maintained by a trusted vendor rather than writing its own. What can it use?
choices: A CloudWatch composite alarm that blocks traffic when it is triggered
A rule set from an AWS Security Partner via the AWS WAF Rules Marketplace
An S3 bucket policy that includes a managed condition for blocking bad requests
A Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rule group that filters outbound DNS queries
questions.correctChoice: A rule set from an AWS Security Partner via the AWS WAF Rules Marketplace
questions.explanation: In addition to custom rules, AWS WAF can use rule sets from AWS Security Partners available through the AWS Marketplace.

questions.prompt: A TCP/HTTP application runs on EC2 behind a Network Load Balancer, and the company must filter HTTP requests that contain SQL injection patterns. Which approach is correct?
choices: Enable AWS Shield Standard, which blocks SQL injection
Add a network ACL rule that matches SQL keywords
Place the application behind an ALB or CloudFront and associate AWS WAF with it
Associate the AWS WAF web ACL directly with the Network Load Balancer
questions.correctChoice: Place the application behind an ALB or CloudFront and associate AWS WAF with it
questions.explanation: WAF can be attached to CloudFront, ALBs, API Gateway REST APIs, AppSync and Cognito user pools, not to NLBs. Shield Standard handles DDoS, not injection.

questions.prompt: Which of the following can have an AWS WAF web ACL associated with it?
choices: An Amazon EC2 instance
An Amazon RDS DB instance
An AWS Direct Connect connection
An AWS AppSync GraphQL API
questions.correctChoice: An AWS AppSync GraphQL API
questions.explanation: WAF supports CloudFront, Application Load Balancers, API Gateway REST APIs, AppSync GraphQL APIs and Cognito user pools.

questions.prompt: What is Amazon API Gateway used for?
choices: Distributing static content from edge locations close to users around the world
Streaming large volumes of real-time data into an analytics pipeline for processing
Creating and managing secure APIs that act as a front door to backend services such as Lambda functions
Running containers on a managed platform without managing the underlying servers
questions.correctChoice: Creating and managing secure APIs that act as a front door to backend services such as Lambda functions
questions.explanation: API Gateway sits between clients and multiple backends and provides routing, throttling, logging, caching and request/response handling at any scale.

questions.prompt: A team needs a simple, low-latency, low-cost API that proxies requests to a Lambda function and does not need advanced features such as caching or API keys. Which API Gateway API type fits best?
choices: REST API
GraphQL API
WebSocket API
HTTP API
questions.correctChoice: HTTP API
questions.explanation: HTTP APIs have a simpler feature set, lower latency and lower cost than REST APIs.

questions.prompt: A chat application needs persistent two-way connections between clients and the backend. Which API Gateway API type should be used?
choices: HTTP API
REST API
Private REST API
WebSocket API
questions.correctChoice: WebSocket API
questions.explanation: WebSocket APIs maintain persistent connections for real-time, two-way communication use cases.

questions.prompt: An API must be reachable only from inside a VPC and not exposed to the internet. Which API Gateway option supports this?
choices: An HTTP API with an edge-optimised endpoint
An HTTP API with a regional endpoint
A REST API with an edge-optimised endpoint
A REST API with a private endpoint type
questions.correctChoice: A REST API with a private endpoint type
questions.explanation: Private endpoints are available for REST APIs only. HTTP APIs support only regional endpoints and are public.

questions.prompt: A company sells API access to partners in tiers, such as a free tier limited to a number of requests per day and a premium tier with higher rate limits. It wants API Gateway to identify and throttle each client natively with minimal custom code. Which solution fits?
choices: A WebSocket API with a $default route
An HTTP API with a JWT authoriser and API keys
A REST API with API keys and usage plans
An HTTP API with a Lambda authoriser that implements throttling logic
questions.correctChoice: A REST API with API keys and usage plans
questions.explanation: API keys with per-client rate limits and quotas are native REST API features. HTTP APIs do not support them, so throttling would require custom code.

questions.prompt: A team uses an external OIDC provider and wants API Gateway to validate JSON Web Tokens natively without writing a custom authoriser. Which API type provides this?
choices: HTTP API
REST API, which has a built-in JWT authoriser
Both REST and HTTP APIs identically
Neither, because JWT validation always needs a Lambda function
questions.correctChoice: HTTP API
questions.explanation: HTTP APIs support JWT authorisation natively. REST APIs can support JWTs, but only through a Lambda authoriser.

questions.prompt: A REST API's backend is being overloaded by repeated identical requests. Which API Gateway capability can reduce load and latency?
choices: Enable API caching on the REST API stage
Enable caching on an HTTP API
Add a Route 53 geolocation record
Switch the API to a WebSocket API
questions.correctChoice: Enable API caching on the REST API stage
questions.explanation: REST APIs support caching of responses in the stage. HTTP APIs do not support caching.

questions.prompt: A team built a low-cost HTTP API. They now need canary release deployments, response caching and request validation. What is the correct conclusion?
choices: Enable them by adding API keys to the HTTP API and creating a usage plan
Convert it to a WebSocket API, which includes all three features by default
Enable them in the HTTP API stage settings, because they are available there
These are REST API features, so the API should be implemented as a REST API
questions.correctChoice: These are REST API features, so the API should be implemented as a REST API
questions.explanation: Canary releases, caching and request validation are available on REST APIs but not HTTP APIs. The trade-off is that REST APIs cost more.

questions.prompt: Global users call an API deployed in a single Region. The company wants requests to enter through the nearest CloudFront point of presence, and it also requires per-client usage plans, response caching and a WAF web ACL attached directly to the API. Which API Gateway configuration meets this?
choices: An HTTP API with a regional endpoint
A REST API with an edge-optimised endpoint
A REST API with a private endpoint
A REST API with a regional endpoint and no CloudFront
questions.correctChoice: A REST API with an edge-optimised endpoint
questions.explanation: Edge-optimised endpoints route through CloudFront and exist only for REST APIs, which also provide usage plans, caching and WAF. HTTP APIs are regional only, and private endpoints are not reachable from the internet.

questions.prompt: In an API Gateway REST API, what is the order of processing for a request?
choices: Integration, method request, method response, integration request, integration response
Method request, integration request, integration, integration response, method response
Method request, integration, integration request, method response, integration response
Integration request, method request, integration, method response, integration response
questions.correctChoice: Method request, integration request, integration, integration response, method response
questions.explanation: The client request is processed by the method request, passed to the integration request, sent to the integration, and the result is handled by the integration response and then the method response.

questions.prompt: A company wants to protect an API Gateway API with AWS WAF. Which API type allows a WAF web ACL to be associated directly?
choices: Neither, because WAF only supports CloudFront
REST API
Both REST API and HTTP API
HTTP API
questions.correctChoice: REST API
questions.explanation: AWS WAF can be attached to REST API stages. HTTP APIs do not support WAF.

questions.prompt: A company must restrict a REST API so that only requests from a specific set of IP address ranges and one specific VPC endpoint are accepted. Which API Gateway feature supports this?
choices: A request mapping template
A resource policy on the REST API
An API key with a usage plan
A JWT authoriser on an HTTP API
questions.correctChoice: A resource policy on the REST API
questions.explanation: Resource policies are available on REST APIs and can allow or deny based on source IP ranges, VPC endpoints and accounts. HTTP APIs do not support resource policies.

questions.prompt: A microservice runs in a private subnet and is registered in AWS Cloud Map. A team wants a low-cost API Gateway API that integrates privately with it through a VPC link. Which API type supports the Cloud Map integration?
choices: REST API with an edge-optimised endpoint
HTTP API
WebSocket API
REST API
questions.correctChoice: HTTP API
questions.explanation: HTTP APIs support private integrations with ALB, NLB and AWS Cloud Map. REST APIs support private integrations with NLB and ALB but not Cloud Map.

questions.prompt: A team needs API Gateway to reject malformed requests and transform request bodies before they reach a Lambda backend, to reduce unneeded backend invocations. Which approach meets this?
choices: An HTTP API with API caching enabled
An HTTP API with request validation and request body transformation
A WebSocket API with a $default route
A REST API with request validation and request body transformation
questions.correctChoice: A REST API with request validation and request body transformation
questions.explanation: Request validation and request body transformation are REST API features. HTTP APIs only support parameter transformation.

questions.prompt: Which AWS services can an HTTP API integrate with directly, apart from Lambda?
choices: A limited set, including SQS, EventBridge, Kinesis Data Streams, AppConfig and Step Functions
Only Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB, through direct service integrations
None, because only Lambda functions and HTTP endpoints can be used as integrations
Any AWS service, through the same AWS service integration that REST APIs provide
questions.correctChoice: A limited set, including SQS, EventBridge, Kinesis Data Streams, AppConfig and Step Functions
questions.explanation: HTTP APIs support a limited set of AWS service integrations (for example EventBridge, SQS, AppConfig, Kinesis Data Streams and Step Functions). REST APIs support the broader set.

questions.prompt: A developer changes a REST API's method but clients still see the old behaviour. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The stage must first be converted to a $default stage
The API has not been deployed to the stage
HTTP APIs are required for changes to take effect
REST API changes deploy automatically but need a CloudFront invalidation
questions.correctChoice: The API has not been deployed to the stage
questions.explanation: A REST API must be deployed to a stage before changes become available. HTTP APIs, by contrast, can auto-deploy the $default stage.

questions.prompt: Which statement about deployments is true for HTTP APIs?
choices: Auto-deployment is available and is the default for the $default stage
Deployments always require a canary configuration to be defined first
They do not support stages at all and have a single fixed version
Changes can only be deployed by manually creating a deployment each time
questions.correctChoice: Auto-deployment is available and is the default for the $default stage
questions.explanation: HTTP APIs support automatic deployments to the default stage, while still allowing user-controlled deployments.

questions.prompt: How can an existing OpenAPI 3 definition be used with API Gateway?
choices: It can only be used with WebSocket APIs
It can be imported when creating a REST or HTTP API
It can only be used with AppSync
It can be used only after being converted to GraphQL
questions.correctChoice: It can be imported when creating a REST or HTTP API
questions.explanation: OpenAPI 3 files can be imported to create REST and HTTP APIs, and AWS extensions allow API Gateway-specific features to be defined in the file.

questions.prompt: In which formats can an OpenAPI definition be written?
choices: HCL or TOML
GraphQL SDL only
XML or CSV
JSON or YAML
questions.correctChoice: JSON or YAML
questions.explanation: OpenAPI definitions are expressed in JSON or YAML.

questions.prompt: A REST API needs detailed execution logs, AWS X-Ray tracing and the ability to test method invocations from the console. Which API type provides these features?
choices: REST API
Both, with identical features
WebSocket API only
HTTP API
questions.correctChoice: REST API
questions.explanation: Execution logs, X-Ray tracing and test invocations are REST API features and are not available on HTTP APIs.

questions.prompt: What is AWS Firewall Manager used for?
choices: Resolving DNS queries between on-premises networks and VPCs through forwarding rules
Centrally configuring and managing firewall rules, such as WAF rules and security groups, across accounts and applications
Replacing AWS WAF with a faster rules engine that is managed separately in each Region and account
Caching content at edge locations so that users receive responses from a nearby location
questions.correctChoice: Centrally configuring and managing firewall rules, such as WAF rules and security groups, across accounts and applications
questions.explanation: Firewall Manager applies protections such as AWS WAF, Shield Advanced, security groups, Network Firewall and DNS Firewall policies centrally across an organisation.

questions.prompt: A security team created an AWS Firewall Manager security policy but it is not applied to resources in several member accounts. The accounts are in the organisation and the administrator account is configured. Which missing prerequisite is the most likely cause?
choices: AWS Config is not enabled in those accounts and Regions
AWS Shield Standard is not enabled in those accounts
The accounts have no CloudFront distribution
The accounts have no Route 53 hosted zone
questions.correctChoice: AWS Config is not enabled in those accounts and Regions
questions.explanation: Firewall Manager requires an AWS Organisation, a designated Firewall Manager administrator and AWS Config enabled for the accounts and Regions in scope. Some policy types also need AWS RAM.

questions.prompt: A company with many AWS accounts wants every ALB in every current and future account in its organisation to have the same WAF rules, enforced centrally and without manual setup in each account. What should it do?
choices: Create a web ACL in each account manually and attach it to each ALB
Create a Route 53 Profile for the organisation
Create an AWS Firewall Manager WAF policy scoped to the organisation
Use AWS Shield Standard, which applies WAF rules automatically
questions.correctChoice: Create an AWS Firewall Manager WAF policy scoped to the organisation
questions.explanation: Firewall Manager policies can be applied across accounts in an AWS Organisation and apply to new accounts and resources automatically.

questions.prompt: A security team wants one central place to manage security group rules, AWS WAF rules, AWS Network Firewall rules and Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rule groups across all accounts. Which service is designed for this?
choices: AWS Config conformance packs only
AWS Shield Advanced
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Firewall Manager
questions.correctChoice: AWS Firewall Manager
questions.explanation: Firewall Manager can manage WAF, Shield Advanced, security groups, network access controls, Network Firewall and DNS Firewall policies. Config is used under the hood but does not manage all these controls directly.

questions.prompt: What is a main advantage of GraphQL over a traditional REST API for clients?
choices: It removes the need for any backend data source, because the schema stores data
It only works with relational databases, because queries are translated to SQL
It guarantees lower cost than any REST API, because it is billed per field
Clients can request exactly the nested data they need in a single query
questions.correctChoice: Clients can request exactly the nested data they need in a single query
questions.explanation: With GraphQL the query defines the exact shape of the data needed, reducing over-fetching and the need for multiple versioned endpoints.

questions.prompt: Which AWS service is a fully managed GraphQL service?
choices: AWS Step Functions
AWS AppSync
Amazon API Gateway HTTP API
Amazon CloudFront
questions.correctChoice: AWS AppSync
questions.explanation: AppSync is the managed GraphQL service, using resolvers to connect schema fields to data sources.

questions.prompt: In GraphQL, which operation type is used to create, update or delete data?
choices: Subscription
Resolver
Mutation
Query
questions.correctChoice: Mutation
questions.explanation: Queries read data, mutations change data, and subscriptions deliver live updates from the server to clients.

questions.prompt: How does AppSync support real-time updates pushed to clients?
choices: Through CloudFront Functions
Through GraphQL subscriptions
Through Route 53 latency records
Through S3 event notifications
questions.correctChoice: Through GraphQL subscriptions
questions.explanation: Subscriptions let AppSync push live updates from the server to connected clients.

questions.prompt: In AppSync, what connects a field in a GraphQL schema to a data source?
choices: A usage plan
A resolver attached to the field
A Lambda@Edge viewer request function
A health check
questions.correctChoice: A resolver attached to the field
questions.explanation: Resolvers attached to fields in types implement the query, mutation and subscription operations against data sources.

questions.prompt: A mobile backend must expose a single GraphQL API that combines order data in DynamoDB, product search in OpenSearch and an existing third-party REST service, with minimal custom server code. What is the best fit?
choices: AWS AppSync with resolvers on DynamoDB, OpenSearch and HTTP data sources
Three separate API Gateway REST APIs, with the client merging the results
An API Gateway WebSocket API with a $default route
CloudFront with three custom origins
questions.correctChoice: AWS AppSync with resolvers on DynamoDB, OpenSearch and HTTP data sources
questions.explanation: AppSync can aggregate multiple data sources, including DynamoDB, OpenSearch, Lambda, HTTP endpoints, EventBridge and RDS, behind a single GraphQL API.

questions.prompt: Several teams each own a separate AppSync GraphQL API. The company wants client applications to use one endpoint that exposes all of them while the teams keep owning their own APIs. Which AppSync feature fits?
choices: API key authorisation
Per-resolver caching
A custom domain name only
Merged APIs
questions.correctChoice: Merged APIs
questions.explanation: A merged API combines multiple GraphQL APIs so they act as one, while each team can keep its source API.

questions.prompt: A mobile team's REST API is repeatedly changed and versioned because different clients need different subsets of nested data, and the client makes several calls per screen. The team wants clients to ask for exactly the fields they need. Which option is the best solution?
choices: API Gateway REST API with caching
A CloudFront distribution with a Lambda@Edge origin request function
API Gateway HTTP API with more routes for each screen
AWS AppSync with a GraphQL schema
questions.correctChoice: AWS AppSync with a GraphQL schema
questions.explanation: GraphQL lets the client define the shape of the data in a query, which avoids over-fetching and many versioned endpoints.

questions.prompt: A collaboration app needs to push live updates to clients when data in DynamoDB changes, with a typed schema and minimal custom connection management. Which approach is the best fit?
choices: A CloudFront distribution with websockets enabled
An API Gateway HTTP API with Lambda integration
AppSync GraphQL subscriptions with a DynamoDB data source
An API Gateway REST API with polling clients
questions.correctChoice: AppSync GraphQL subscriptions with a DynamoDB data source
questions.explanation: AppSync supports real-time APIs via GraphQL subscriptions with managed connections. REST APIs and HTTP APIs have no persistent connection model.

questions.prompt: Users of an AppSync API authenticate with a third-party OpenID Connect identity provider and the company does not use Amazon Cognito. Which authorisation mode is the best fit?
choices: AWS IAM
API key
Amazon Cognito user pools
OpenID Connect
questions.correctChoice: OpenID Connect
questions.explanation: AppSync supports API key, IAM, Cognito user pools, Lambda and OpenID Connect authorisation. OIDC validates tokens from an external provider, whereas Cognito requires a user pool.

questions.prompt: An AppSync API has a few expensive resolvers that read rarely changing data from DynamoDB. The team wants to cache only those resolvers' results. Which statement is correct?
choices: Use full request caching, which can't be limited to specific resolvers
Use per-resolver caching, which is serverless and needs no cache instance
Use per-resolver caching, which requires provisioning an on-demand cache instance
Enable caching on an HTTP API instead, because AppSync cannot cache
questions.correctChoice: Use per-resolver caching, which requires provisioning an on-demand cache instance
questions.explanation: AppSync supports no caching, full request caching and per-resolver caching. Caching uses a provisioned cache instance rather than a serverless option.

questions.prompt: A company has a global web store with cacheable product images and pages, plus a UDP-based voice service. It wants edge caching for the web content and accelerated routing to healthy Regional endpoints for the voice service. Which design meets this?
choices: Route 53 latency-based routing for both
CloudFront for the web content and Global Accelerator for the UDP service
CloudFront for both
Global Accelerator for both, with the web content cached by Global Accelerator
questions.correctChoice: CloudFront for the web content and Global Accelerator for the UDP service
questions.explanation: CloudFront caches HTTP(S) content at the edge but doesn't handle UDP. Global Accelerator doesn't cache, but accelerates TCP and UDP traffic to healthy endpoints.
